query:
After the group confirmed there would be a post-hike pub visit, one member's agreement contained a condition that revealed their real position on the trip. What did that condition signal about their actual attitude, and how would you have known from the way they phrased it?

Options:
A. Dev
B. Jonah
C. Marcus
D. Priya
context:
[1] (about=Jonah, episodic, t4 @2025-10-19T19:34:00) this is fine, I'll still be recovering from the walk. someone tell me now what pub is near the bunkhouse in Hope because post-hike priorities need to be settled in advance
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t6 @2025-10-26T18:12:00) Actually booked. Confirmation email sent to everyone including Simone. I also checked there's a pub within 400 metres of the bunkhouse for Jonah's post-hike requirements. The pub is called the Cheshire Cheese and has a 4.1 on Google.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Jonah, group-interaction, t4 @2025-10-19T19:15:00) Jonah asks about pub near bunkhouse in Hope for post-hike priorities.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) Hike was not good; ankles hurt, mud, view only nice for four minutes before cloud came in.
[5] (about=Simone, episodic, t10 @2025-11-09T19:48:00) December 19th. I fly January 6th. So there's time to do something properly before I go. I'd like that, if everyone's up for it. Something quiet. Not a party, just us.
agent_answer:
**B. Jonah**

Jonah’s agreement came with the condition that he’d “still be recovering from the walk,” and he asked for the pub to be settled in advance. That signaled he saw the hike as physically draining — something to get through and recover from — rather than something he was genuinely enthusiastic about. You can tell from his phrasing: “this is fine” sounds grudging, and “post-hike priorities” frames the pub as a practical recovery need, not a celebration.

query:
When Marcus asked the group to confirm plans for New Year, one member responded in a way that had become a recognisable pattern across multiple sessions. What did that response reveal about how they actually approach group commitments, and what in how they phrased it — across the whole conversation — makes that visible?

Options:
A. Jonah
B. Dev
C. Marcus
D. Priya
context:
[1] (about=Jonah, episodic, t13 @2025-11-23T19:15:00) right so Marcus it's nearly December and you have not mentioned the trivia night and I need to know if we're doing this or if 2025 is the year the institution dies
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2025-11-23T19:16:00) I've been writing the question cards. I have a full round on post-war European history and a wildcard round I'm calling 'did this actually happen or did Jonah make it up'. The institution will not die.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t4 @2025-10-19T19:15:00) Group agreed to dinner on Saturday 25th October for Peak District debrief; Italian again but a different quiet place.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t4 @2025-10-19T19:15:00) Priya agrees to pub as long as no hill on Sunday morning.
[5] (about=GROUP, said_by=Simone, group-interaction, t0 @2025-10-05T18:30:00) Agreed to dinner at new Italian place on Renfield Street on Friday; confirm by Wednesday.
agent_answer:
A. Jonah.

Jonah’s response is the recognisable pattern: instead of confirming his own plans, he puts the burden back on Marcus — “you have not mentioned the trivia night,” “I need to know if we’re doing this” — and then escalates it dramatically: “or if 2025 is the year the institution dies.”

That phrasing shows how he actually approaches group commitments: he waits for someone else to prove the plan is real before he engages, and pressures the organiser rather than stating his own availability.

query:
After the Peak District trip, the group debriefed and one member confirmed they had run on the descent. What did that confirmation signal about their actual preference for the kind of group trip this was, and what in their phrasing reveals that this was more than just neutral attendance?

Options:
A. Marcus
B. Priya
C. Jonah
D. Dev
context:
[1] (about=Dev, episodic, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) The descent was good.
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2025-11-09T19:32:00) It was a good training run. I'll be honest with you, that descent was the best I've felt on a run in months. Also the bunkhouse kitchen was better than advertised. The scrambled eggs situation at 7am was a genuine triumph.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Jonah, group-interaction, t8 @2025-11-02T18:46:00) Group hiking order agreed: Dev and Marcus up front, Jonah and Marcus (self) in middle, Priya and Simone rear guard.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) City trip proposal to be voted on in January.
[5] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t10 @2025-11-09T19:31:00) Hike was not good; ankles hurt, mud, view only nice for four minutes before cloud came in.
agent_answer:
A. Marcus

Marcus is the one who confirmed running the descent: he called it “a good training run” and added, “that descent was the best I've felt on a run in months.”

That confirmation signals that Marcus preferred this kind of group trip as a **training/active running trip**, not just a neutral social outing. His phrasing shows more than neutral attendance through the personal, invested language: “I'll be honest with you” and “the best I've felt on a run in months” reveal genuine enthusiasm and emotional stake in the experience, rather than simply turning up.
